After the arrest, she was initially charged with obstructing official business. Operating a vehicle under the influence, commonly known as OVI, known as OVI in Ohio, failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer, and a secondary OVI charge for a breathed alcohol content over the legal limit. When prosecutors formally filed the case, two additional charges were added, driving under suspension and a minor misdemeanor for failing to have proper headlights turned on. One month later, she pleaded guilty to the primary first offense OVI charge and the judge adjudicated her guilty. The remaining five charges were dismissed. She was sentenced to 180 days in jail, with 177 days suspended, followed by two years of community control. Her driver's license was suspended for two years, though she was granted limited driving privileges for medical and vocational purposes. She was also ordered to complete a three-day AIP class and to pay $941 in fines, court costs, and attorney fees. Following her sentencing, a bench warrant was issued for her arrest in March 26, after she failed to appear for a hearing related to fines and court costs.

After the arrest, she was initially charged with obstructing official business.
Operating a vehicle under the influence, commonly known as OVI,
known as OVI in Ohio, failure to comply with an order or signal of a police officer, and a
secondary OVI charge for a breathed alcohol content over the legal limit. When prosecutors formally
filed the case, two additional charges were added, driving under suspension and a minor misdemeanor
for failing to have proper headlights turned on. One month later, she pleaded guilty to the primary
first offense OVI charge and the judge adjudicated her guilty. The remaining five charges were
dismissed. She was sentenced to 180 days in jail, with 177 days suspended, followed by two
years of community control. Her driver's license was suspended for two years, though she was granted
limited driving privileges for medical and vocational purposes. She was also ordered to complete a
three-day AIP class and to pay $941 in fines, court costs, and attorney fees. Following her
sentencing, a bench warrant was issued for her arrest in March 26, after she failed to appear
for a hearing related to fines and court costs.
